approval.note: OTC NSAID; chemoprevention is off-label. Label queried is a low-dose (81 mg) product.

claims.text: Mechanistic interception angle: a phenotypic screen found aspirin (and resveratrol) selectively eliminate tetraploid cells - the genomically metastable precursor state to aneuploidy - by slowing cell-cycle progression and triggering intrinsic apoptosis. In MVA, where aneuploid cells arise continuously, preferential pruning of the pre-/aneuploid compartment is the Axis-C interception hypothesis.

Strongest clinical chemoprevention precedent: in the randomised double-blind CAPP2 trial (861 Lynch-syndrome patients, 600 mg aspirin daily), colorectal cancer incidence was reduced (ITT HR 0.65, 95% CI 0.43-0.97) at 10-year follow-up - RCT evidence that chronic aspirin prevents cancer in a hereditary predisposition syndrome.

Honest bound on c2: the CAPP2 effect was specific to colorectal cancer (mismatch-repair-deficiency biology); non-colorectal Lynch cancers showed no ITT effect. MVA-associated tumours (rhabdomyosarcoma, Wilms, leukaemias) arise from chromosomal instability, not MMR loss - so the clinical analogy is weak and mechanism-dependent on c1.

Tetraploid elimination as cancer interception is mechanism-consistent with the aneuploidy-selective killing field (AICAR/17-AAG/chloroquine class evidence), but no aspirin experiment exists in a BUB1B/MVA model.

pediatric.label_source: openFDA drug/label set_id 0058175f-3474-40c3-a046-6cfaec86d84b (effective 2024-04-16); low-dose (81 mg) OTC product
pediatric.approved_pediatric_indication: None for chronic use. Label directions: 'children under 12 years: consult a doctor'. Label carries the Reye's syndrome warning (see key_risks).
pediatric.label_pediatric_dosing_fact: No pediatric chemoprevention dosing exists; OTC label dosing is for analgesia only.
key_risks: Reye's syndrome (label warning verbatim): 'Children and teenagers who have or are recovering from chicken pox or flu-like symptoms should not use this product' - a real, label-level pediatric hazard for chronic daily use.
Stomach bleeding warning (NSAID class) plus allergy alert; cumulative GI/renal caution.
Antiplatelet effect: bleeding-risk interactions (e.g. with dasatinib's platelet inhibition if combined).
Chronic daily dosing in a child would be an unprecedented preventive exposure; the only RCT evidence is in adults.
monitoring: Withhold during varicella/influenza-like illness (Reye's precaution, label)

celegans.expected: weak rationale; low cost to include in screen

fibroblasts.assay: chronic low-dose aspirin on MVA patient fibroblasts
fibroblasts.readout: tetraploid/aneuploid cell fraction over passages (FISH/scDNA-seq), apoptosis markers
fibroblasts.expected: enrichment for euploid fraction if tetraploid pruning is active

verdict_reason: Cheapest possible cancer-interception lever with a real mechanism (selective tetraploid-cell elimination, PMID:24516128) and the only RCT-grade chemoprevention precedent in a hereditary syndrome (CAPP2, PMID:32534647). But the RCT benefit was colorectal-cancer-specific in MMR-deficient Lynch syndrome - mechanism, not syndrome, must carry the extrapolation to MVA's sarcoma/nephroblastoma spectrum; pediatric chronic use hits the label's Reye's-syndrome warning; and no MVA-model data exist. Kept as an adjunct consideration alongside structured cancer surveillance rather than a lead candidate.
